source: Derived from recorded native public AWS responses; no inferred private CloudFormation calls

execution.writes: Two unique custom buses, one exact-source-ARN-scoped SQS queue, one stack containing one explicitly named AWS::Events::Rule, and one same-name native collision sentinel on the second owned bus
execution.default_bus: Neither mutated nor used for event publishing; reverse custom-bus migration was chosen instead

facts: EventBusName update is documented as Some interruptions; omission selects default bus.
Name update is documented as Replacement.
Ref is documented as event rule ID; example names do not establish the custom-bus physical-ID format.
Arn is a documented GetAtt attribute.
PutRule creates or updates the named rule on the specified event bus.
For an existing rule, unspecified arguments replace previous values with null rather than retaining them.
PutRule ignores supplied tags for existing rules; tags are updated through TagResource/UntagResource.
Rule changes may require a short period before incoming events match.

public_registry_schema.evidence: findings.schema_contract and calls[label=rule-public-registry-schema] in the capture
public_registry_schema.interpretation_limit: EventBusName is not in createOnlyProperties, but this does not establish native update identity or private handler sequencing.

public_stack_events: UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS: Requested update requires the creation of a new physical resource; hence creating one.
UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS on new bus|name: Resource creation Initiated

transitions.label: migrate-second
transitions.second_rule: Present, ENABLED, stack-target attached with the same queue ARN and retry policy

transitions.label: missing-destination
transitions.failure_message: Event bus stackd-cfn-rule-cee0647e0583-missing does not exist.
transitions.first_rule: Original rule, targets, Ref, Arn and tags preserved

transitions.label: owned-destination-collision
transitions.failure_message: Resource of type 'AWS::Events::Rule' with identifier 'stackd-cfn-rule-cee0647e0583-rule' already exists.
transitions.first_rule: Original rule, targets, Ref, Arn and tags preserved
transitions.second_rule: Probe-owned native sentinel preserved: DISABLED, collision source pattern, native-sentinel target and collision-sentinel tag unchanged

routing.method: One unique-marker PutEvents entry to each owned custom bus after each transition; actual ReceiveMessage bodies and message deletions retained
routing.queue_policy: events.amazonaws.com may SendMessage only with SourceArn equal to the exact two owned rule ARNs and SourceAccount 000000000000
routing.limit: Positive delivery was observed for every active-bus sample. No inactive-bus sample was received within the bounded window; this is not a proof of permanent non-delivery.

cleanup.stack: DELETE_COMPLETE by exact ARN; stack name absence verified
cleanup.rules: Stack-owned source rule absent after stack deletion; exact destination collision targets removed, sentinel deleted, absence verified
cleanup.custom_buses: Both empty custom buses deleted; DescribeEventBus returned ResourceNotFoundException for each
cleanup.cleanup_only_recovery: Successfully re-read the deleted stack history and confirmed absence of rules, queue and both buses without recreating resources
cleanup.history_limit: Deleted stack ARN and CloudFormation event history persist in AWS and are not claimed absent

limits: Native results establish custom-bus Ref as busName|ruleName, not the local engine's previously assumed rule-name-only identity.
Public stack events describe physical-resource creation/deletion; direct native PutRule/PutTargets/RemoveTargets/DeleteRule ordering inside CloudFormation was not captured.
The collision was strictly probe-owned. The result does not authorize touching unrelated same-name rules.
No default-bus migration, cross-account resources, scheduled rules, foreign ownership-token behavior or mid-flight crash recovery is calibrated.
